questions.question: SahayaMart's AI Transformation SahayaMart, a growing Indian retail / chain, plans to introduce an AI system across its physical stores and online platform. The proposed system will study purchase records to forecast stock requirements, assist customers through a chatbot and help store managers make faster operational decisions. The management expects the project to reduce stock-outs, improve customer service and support business growth. A pilot study, however, reveals several concerns. Customer records contain missing entries, duplicate profiles and outdated contact details. Some stores have reliable internet connectivity and modern systems, while others use older computers. Employees fear that the technology may replace their jobs, and many managers have limited knowledge of AI. The company has not yet clearly assigned responsibility for checking AI-generated decisions. The pilot chatbot also performs differently across customer groups because its training data does not adequately represent all regional languages. Customers are not clearly informed about how their purchase histories and conversations will be used. SahayaMart therefore decides that employees must review important AI decisions, customers must receive clear information about data use, and staff must be trained to work effectively with the new system. Answer the following questions based on the case study: 1. Identify the major challenges that SahayaMart may face while implementing AI. Support your answer with evidence from the case. 2. Examine the bias and data-privacy concerns in the proposed AI system. Suggest suitable responsible AI measures. 3. Explain how human-AI collaboration can help SahayaMart introduce the system without weakening employee roles or managerial accountability.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
